image_prompts.1: Use case: identity-preserve / compositing. Create ONE photorealistic cinematic 16:9 production reference still for Scene52 part1: Serega boarding his OWN flat personal spaceship in a large Imperial hangar. Image1 is the exact personal craft design; image2 is its established hangar placement, landing gear, single side doorway and short folding ramp; image3 is Serega exact face, thinning light-brown hair and deep plum layered robe identity; image4 is the previous repair scene's real ending, only for hangar lighting and the separate BROKEN winged Lambda shuttle in the distant background. Main foreground subject: the same broad dark graphite very LOW flat wedge craft from images1/2, shallow angular canopy, warm thin side lights, original hull paneling, no tall dorsal fin, no folding wings, no person on roof. Preserve the existing side hatch and ramp exactly. Serega, adult pale middle-aged man, is midway UP that ramp, side/three-quarter view, his right foot on the next ramp tread, head turned slightly toward the doorway, stern deadpan face readable at medium scale, hands relaxed; only ONE Serega. Make him human-sized relative to the doorway. In the far background on another service position show the pale Lambda shuttle from image4 with its detached wing panel on the floor and small repair crew, clearly a SECOND DIFFERENT ship; no blending of designs. Wide 35mm ground-level 3/4 framing with the personal craft nose pointing screen right and entire ramp visible, the hangar's open starfield/planet aperture and vertical practical strip lights. Real metal, believable scale, cool hangar light and warm ramp light. Keep the ship cleanly readable and the action immediately understandable. No text, arrows, collage, border, watermark, extra main characters, lightsabers or weapons in Serega's hands.
image_prompts.2: Use case: precise-object-edit / cinematic compositing. ONE photorealistic 16:9 reference still for Scene52 part2, an exciting physical takeoff from the SAME hangar. Image1 is the exact personal craft design authority. Image2 is the exact hangar and ground layout. Reposition the SAME broad low dark graphite wedge craft so it is visibly flying 2-3 metres above the hangar floor, accelerating toward the huge open space aperture. It must have the same shallow angular cockpit glazing, flush low roof, original panel seams and horizontal warm side lights; no tall fin, no Lambda folding wings. Side hatch and ramp completely CLOSED and flush; landing gear retracting naturally into the belly, not dragging on floor. Camera is a dynamic rear-side three-quarter tracking view at low altitude: enough side/top is visible to identify the craft from the references, rear propulsion glow stays attached to original engine positions, the open hangar aperture and blue planet limb ahead. The floor drops visibly beneath the ship with strong parallax lines and subtle heat distortion; directional background motion blur only, crisp ship silhouette. Serega remains fully inside the enclosed cockpit and is not visible on any exterior surface. No other foreground ships, no explosion, no laser battle, no decorative giant engine or extra propulsion pods. Film-grade metal and practical illumination, exhilarating forward momentum, physically credible clearance at the doorway. No text, diagram, montage, letterboxing or watermark.
image_prompts.3: Use case: precise-object-edit / cinematic compositing. Produce ONE photorealistic 16:9 film reference still for Scene52 part3: a thrilling external fly-by of the EXACT cruiser in Image1, with Serega's EXACT personal craft from Image2. Image1 is the absolute cruiser-design authority, not generic inspiration: preserve its immense grey triangular wedge hull, layered stepped central superstructure, raised wide bridge platform with TWO spherical domes, edge trenches and lit windows, matching bow and proportions. Image2 is a DIFFERENT MUCH SMALLER personal craft: low flat dark graphite wedge, shallow angular canopy, warm horizontal edge lights; keep this craft recognizable with no dorsal fin and no Lambda wings. Composition: the giant cruiser fills the upper and right background, sharp and readable in its entirety; the small craft is near the camera in the lower-left foreground, banking along the cruiser's near-side trench on a clear SAFE outward arc around the bow. Give spectacular depth with huge hull plates and tiny cruiser windows diminishing behind it; the personal craft is tens of metres long while the cruiser is over a kilometre, never equal-sized. The small craft occupies about one fifth of frame width because it is much closer to camera; its flight arc follows the cruiser, not an attack. Tilted tracking-camera composition, strong parallax, black starfield and cool raking starlight, restrained warm engine glow and the exact dark metal design. Closed ramp/hatch, fully stowed gear; pilot entirely inside, nobody on roof or exterior. Only these two main ships, no battle, explosions, energy ribbons or lasers. Do not substitute a different Star Destroyer, redesign the bridge tower, or merge the two ships. No captions, borders, collage, arrows or watermark.
image_prompts.4: Use case: cinematic compositing. ONE photorealistic 16:9 film production reference still for Scene52 part4: exhilarating descent toward a Tatooine desert spaceport town. Image1 is the ABSOLUTE design authority for Serega's personal low flat dark graphite wedge spaceship. Image2 establishes the EXACT destination town: preserve its sun-bleached sand-coloured rounded adobe walls, clustered domed roofs, arch doorways, slim moisture-vaporator towers, fabric market awnings and surrounding dunes. Show the same ship in a fast descending BANKED TURN over a dune crest, its nose aiming toward the outskirts of that town in the middle distance. Three-quarter trailing aerial camera, strong diagonal composition and clear readable ship silhouette, expansive golden dunes sweeping below, hot atmospheric haze over the adobe city, a visible open sandy landing field outside town. The city is a LIVED-IN SPACEPORT, no ancient ruins. Ship fully airborne several tens of metres above the sand, all landing gear stowed, side hatch/ramp closed flush. Maintain the exact broad low hull, shallow canopy and side light strips, no tall fin or folding wings, no extra engines; no rider or silhouette on roof. Directional background blur and sand lifting behind the low flight track communicate speed, but no fire or crash. Camera sees both destination and flight direction without being a top-down map. Harsh late-morning desert sunlight, blue pale sky, realistic granular sand and weathered surfaces. No text, arrows, collage, border, watermark, fight, worm or weapons. Serega is inside the cockpit and unseen.
